policy: Visible-state conservative v2: secure tribute first; use remaining safe/full-charge Frenzy; low expected capital at risk when short; at most two low-value spare trades, visible scored relics/replacements, one reroll then buy again, limited merchant purchases, manual legal ward use.
policy_limits: One hand-authored strategy and this small common-seed sample are an exploratory command probe, not player win-rate or calibrated balance.
Slots4/8 are pre-unlocked entitlement cohorts, not natural rewarded-slot unlock behavior or its time cost.

Ward treatment simulates one verified-earned test callback at the first legal merchant visit, not an SDK/video/ad conversion test. Inventory wards are fungible; individual free-ward causality is not inferred.
Fresh profiles; original permanent unlocks earned only within this one contract. No carry-over unlock population is modeled.
No post-start injected money, probability, relics, levels, swords or skipped rounds; all accepted actions use Session commands and a memory SaveStore.
Exact cooldown pacing models continuous legal input and frozen menu time, without human reaction, watch time, device latency or native persistence failures.
Fixed relic scores/trade caps and greedy tribute/forge rules are imperfect. Failure may reflect this policy, not game impossibility.
The probe stops after the natural21-day ending; extension mastery and full population retention/monetization are untested.
Censored guards and command errors are separate outcomes and are never relabeled natural failures. No automatic balance changes are made.
pilot_note: A one-seed availability pilot was discarded before the official sample. It exposed an overly restrictive actor rule requiring an extra spare sword beyond secured tribute, which suppressed all trades. V2 permits trading the last unmarked low-value spare only while marked tribute still covers quota; no game rules changed.

reproducibility_check.note: Six additional replays validate reproducibility; they do not enlarge the twenty independent common seeds.

resolved_preflight_defect.defect: Buying a sword into an empty cabinet added the sword without selecting it, so Session validation rejected an otherwise legal rescue purchase.
resolved_preflight_defect.fix: AddSword now calls FixSelection after insertion. Owner added empty-cabinet purchase/save-reopen regression.

ward_comparator: Free per-contract earned ward off versus on; original merchant-purchased wards remain available in both cohorts. The on arm uses a simulated earned receipt, not a real advertisement.

interpretation.scope: Exploratory legal-command and resource-closure probe; this frozen actor is not a model of the real player population. No game parameters changed.
interpretation.observed: All six cohorts naturally failed in this sample (0/20 complete each), with no command errors/censoring after the empty-cabinet fix. That does not establish a true player completion probability of zero or game impossibility.
interpretation.policy_bottleneck: The actor stops dangerous forging once current tribute is covered and usually delivers all or most developed blades. It rarely creates spare low-value swords for credits (mean total trades 0.75/1.45/1.65 for2/4/8 slots), so added slot capacity is often not populated. Its safe-burst handling does not compensate for limited long-term blade banking or future-build planning.
interpretation.ward_observation: The free grant frequently replaces an otherwise affordable day3 paid ward. In the two-slot pairs its paths match while merchant spending falls by1100 gold; no conclusion about real ad demand follows. Later extra spending/path changes can affect failure round; inventory is fungible.
interpretation.slot_observation: More capacity changes purchases and replacement choices, so effects are not monotonic under a fixed greedy policy. Slightly earlier/later failure in twenty paired seeds is not evidence to nerf/buff capacity or probability.
interpretation.next_validation: Keep game parameters frozen. A separately specified strategy that deliberately banks a growth blade or develops a stronger endogenous credit loop, and human playtests across more than one contract/unlock population, would address the observed policy coverage gaps before balance decisions.
interpretation.sample_size_decision: Do not expand this same actor merely to manufacture clears or precise rates.120 completed contracts plus6 reproducibility replays are sufficient for this command-availability/resource-accounting pass; they are insufficient for population balance or monetization inference.
